title: Job titles of the future: Delivery drone air traffic controller
gist: Profile of Trevor Wischnewsky, a remote pilot in command at drone-delivery firm FlyTrex in Dallas, who supervises up to 10 automated hexacopter deliveries at once while the area's UTM network lets FlyTrex, Zipline, Amazon and Wing drones share positions to avoid collisions.

insights.claim: Drone delivery is competitive in Dallas, where FlyTrex coordinates traffic with delivery drones from Zipline, Amazon and Alphabet's Wing, serving homes and businesses within a three-mile radius.
insights.speaker: Eamon Whalen
insights.so_what: Dallas is a live multi-operator drone-delivery market, a bellwether for commercial scaling.

insights.claim: The Dallas-Fort Worth area is a testing ground for unmanned aircraft systems traffic management (UTM), letting autonomous drones from competing operators share coordinates in real time to avoid collisions beyond the pilot's line of sight.
insights.speaker: Eamon Whalen
insights.so_what: Shared UTM infrastructure is a key enabler for beyond-line-of-sight drone delivery at scale.

insights.claim: One remote pilot in command can supervise up to 10 drones at once, acting as a safety net while automation handles flight.
insights.speaker: Eamon Whalen
insights.so_what: High drone-to-operator ratios improve delivery unit economics.
insights.quote: At his busiest, Wischnewsky will have up to 10 drones on his watch at the same time.
insights.locator: Ability to stay calm under pressure

insights.claim: Weather is the most common hazard, requiring human intervention such as recalling a drone when wind picked up suddenly seconds after takeoff.
insights.speaker: Eamon Whalen
insights.so_what: Weather limits remain an operational constraint on drone delivery reliability.
insights.locator: Ability to stay calm under pressure

insights.claim: FlyTrex requires FAA drone-pilot certification plus a weeks-long FAA-approved training course so operators can take over a drone if needed.
insights.speaker: Eamon Whalen
insights.so_what: Regulatory staffing requirements add labor cost and shape the drone operator workforce.
